overview: Black prepares ...d5 with a Caro-Kann or Slav pawn, so the game usually becomes a Slav-type structure with colours reversed on the tempo. White chooses between Nf3/Nc3 and ...d5 lines that transpose to the Slav or QGD, or g3 and a fianchetto. Quiet, manoeuvring play with few early tactics.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3, Nc3 or g3/Bg2, keeping d4 and e4 options open
Transpose to Slav or Catalan-style set-ups after 2.Nf3 d5 3.e3 or 3.d4

black_ideas.idea: ...d5 supported by c6, then ...Bf5 or ...e6 and ...Nf6
Solid pawn chain with easy development and a sound centre

typical_structures.structure: Slav structure with c6/d5 against c4 and d3 or d4
Exchange on d5 giving a symmetrical or half-open c-file position

character.notes: Quiet Slav-style positions; Black has a solid centre and few weaknesses.

structure.notes: Centre not fixed: transposes to Slav/QGD, English fianchetto structures; flexible.

approach.notes: A reply to 1.c4, not a repertoire system; standard.

level.notes: Clear plans and little theory; fine for Intermediate players.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2.e4
sublines_that_differ.how: Becomes a Caro-Kann like game with extra c4 space for White, sharper.

character.reason: Black builds a Slav-style pawn chain and few forcing lines arise.

soundness.reason: Both sides play standard, sound set-ups.

structure.reason: Pawn centre is undecided and transposes to Slav, QGD or English structures.

approach.reason: A normal reply to the English, not a system or a surprise.

level.reason: Easy plans but transpositions need some Slav knowledge.

plans.reason: Too many transpositions to name one plan.
